title: The Eight Immortals Cross the Sea
text:
The Eight Immortals of Chinese legend were eight very different figures who had each attained immortality: a beggar with an iron crutch and a gourd, a general with a fan, an old man who rode his donkey backward, a scholar with a sword, a young woman with a lotus, a musician with a flute, a wandering singer with a basket of flowers, and a nobleman with castanets.

In the best-known story, they were traveling home from a celestial banquet when they came to the Eastern Sea. They could simply have ridden clouds across. Instead, one of them proposed that each should cross using only his or her own particular magic. So the iron-crutch beggar floated on his crutch or gourd, the general rode his fan, the lady stood on her lotus leaf, and the rest each used their own treasure, and the whole company sailed out over the waves.

In many versions the crossing led to trouble: the son of the Dragon King of the sea seized one of the treasures, and a battle followed between the immortals and the dragons, which only ended through the mediation of a higher power. But the image of the crossing itself became a proverb: when the Eight Immortals cross the sea, each shows his own powers.
lesson: A team does not need everyone to work the same way. Let each member reach the goal with the skills they have, as long as everyone arrives.
source: Ming dynasty drama and the novel Journey to the East (Dongyou ji) by Wu Yuantai
caveat: Details such as each immortal's vehicle and the battle with the dragons vary between versions.
